header.title: AI Tax Filing
header.subtitle: UK tax returns, filed with HMRC by software and an AI agent.
header.description: Bank statements go in, an AI agent reads and sorts every transaction, a person checks the result, and the return goes to HMRC through Making Tax Digital. We build it under your brand and set up the agent for your clients.

intro.title: What you are evaluating
intro.body: A tax return application for the UK with an AI agent built in. It reads bank statements (PDF or CSV), sorts each transaction into the right HMRC category, works out the figures and files with HMRC through Making Tax Digital for Income Tax and for VAT. The agent does the slow reading and sorting. People make the decisions: the client confirms the figures, an accountant can review any line, and nothing is sent to HMRC until someone ticks the declaration. TenthMatrix licenses it to accountancy firms, and each firm offers it to its own clients under the firm's brand.

videos.title: 01 · A landlord with 100 properties, and an AI that learns from last year (with voice)
videos.caption: Jordan files the 2025-26 return with the AI assistant and no accountant step. 274 of 275 transactions are sorted from what Jordan confirmed in 2024-25, with no AI model call; only 1 goes to the AI model and only 1 is flagged. The estimate includes the mortgage interest: £571,273 tax on £1,477,310 property profit, with no Class 4 National Insurance. Jordan confirms the year in one click, connects to HMRC and files. Narrated in a British voice, with subtitles.
videos.thumbnailAlt: AI that learns from last year: a 100-property landlord's tax estimate of £571,272

videos.title: 02 · Landlord Self Assessment, filed with HMRC
videos.caption: A landlord tells the AI assistant about their lets, uploads twelve monthly statements and lets the agent sort 275 transactions. The tax is worked out, the landlord connects to HMRC and the return is filed through Making Tax Digital.
videos.thumbnailAlt: Landlord tax return figures with HMRC's calculation

videos.title: 03 · Landlord VAT return under Making Tax Digital
videos.caption: Every bank line gets a VAT treatment, a rules engine works out the 9 boxes (never the AI), and the return is submitted to HMRC. Partial exemption and the annual adjustment are included.
videos.thumbnailAlt: The 9-box VAT return worked out from coded lines

videos.title: 04 · The AI sorts, an accountant reviews
videos.caption: After the agent has sorted the year, an accountant works through the lines it was unsure of. Each correction is explained on screen, so a practice keeps a qualified person in charge.
videos.thumbnailAlt: Transaction review queue for an accountant

videos.title: 05 · Bank statements to HMRC-ready figures
videos.caption: The landlord picks "Do it with the AI assistant". It asks about mortgage interest, treats residential and commercial loans differently, and updates the estimate as it reads the statements.
videos.thumbnailAlt: AI assistant reading a landlord's bank statements

videos.title: 06 · Sole trader: AI bookkeeping to HMRC filing
videos.caption: A self-employed consultant uploads two statements. The agent keeps personal spending out of the business figures, HMRC works out the tax and the return is filed.
videos.thumbnailAlt: Sole trader return filed with HMRC

videos.title: 07 · Your own branded app for your end customers
videos.caption: The same engine under your brand, for your end customers: sign in, upload, extract, classify, reconcile, calculate and file. Your clients see your name, not ours.
videos.thumbnailAlt: White-label tax return app under your own brand

items.title: Statements in
items.text: The client uploads bank statements as PDF or CSV, or chats with the assistant about their income first.

items.title: The agent sorts
items.text: Each line is sorted into an HMRC category using your rules first, then past decisions, then the model. Doubtful lines are flagged.

items.title: A person checks
items.text: The client or an accountant reviews the flagged lines and confirms the rest. Every figure links back to its transactions.

items.title: HMRC calculates
items.text: The figures go to HMRC, which works out the tax. Nothing is binding yet, and it can be repeated as often as needed.

items.title: Filed
items.text: Someone ticks the declaration and the return is filed through Making Tax Digital. HMRC's receipt is kept with the return.

items.title: Your branded application

items.title: AI agent setup

aiAngle.title: What it does not do
aiAngle.intro: Limits worth knowing before you buy.
points: The AI never calculates the tax or the VAT boxes. A rules engine does, and HMRC confirms.
Nothing is filed without a person confirming the figures and ticking the declaration.
The videos use HMRC's sandbox with test taxpayers. Live filing needs your HMRC production approval, which can take a few weeks.
HMRC does not accept a final declaration before the tax year ends. The app shows the estimate until then.
Speed depends on the model. On our test server, a local model took about two hours to read 12 monthly statements. A GPU or a hosted model is much faster.

items.question: Who buys the application, and who uses it?
items.answer: TenthMatrix licenses it to accountancy firms. Your firm then offers it to your own clients, under your brand, as part of your service. Your accountants and your clients use the same application, each with their own access.

items.question: Can it replace QuickBooks or Xero for our clients?
items.answer: Yes. Clients keep their records, upload bank statements and documents, message your team and file their returns in one application, instead of using QuickBooks, Xero or other accounting software alongside email and Dropbox. During scoping we go through what your clients use today and map it onto the application.

items.question: Are there iPhone and Android apps?
items.answer: Yes. Mobile apps for iPhone and Android, under your firm's brand, are included in the enterprise licence.

items.question: Does the AI file returns on its own?
items.answer: No. The AI reads and sorts transactions. A rules engine works out the figures, HMRC confirms the Income Tax calculation, and nothing is filed until a person confirms the figures and ticks the declaration.

items.question: Can we file live with HMRC today?
items.answer: The videos were recorded in HMRC's sandbox with test taxpayers. Live filing needs HMRC production approval. HMRC is not currently accepting new production requests for 2026–27 MTD Income Tax quarterly update products, so we agree the right route for your firm during scoping.

items.question: Where is client data kept?
items.answer: Hosted in the UK by us, or on your own servers. The agent can run on a hosted model or on a local model, so bank statements never leave your network.

items.question: How is it priced?
items.answer: Your firm takes an enterprise licence, quoted after a 30-minute scoping call and based on how many clients you serve. The branded web application, the mobile apps and the agent setup are part of it.
